None of the U.S. states that sit on the Atlantic coast and have a land area larger than Ohio qualify.  
Ohio’s land area is about **116 000 sq mi**. The Atlantic‑coast states all have smaller areas:

| State | Land area (sq mi) |
|-------|-------------------|
| Maine | 35 385 |
| New Hampshire | 9 104 |
| Vermont | 9 616 |
| Massachusetts | 10 554 |
| Rhode Island | 1 545 |
| Connecticut | 5 543 |
| New York | 54 169 |
| New Jersey | 8 722 |
| Delaware | 1 949 |
| Maryland | 12 406 |
| Virginia | 42 774 |
| North Carolina | 53 819 |
| South Carolina | 32 020 |
| Georgia | 59 425 |
| Florida | 65 755 |

Because none of these coastal states is larger than Ohio and the only state with a higher‑education attainment rate in 2019 (per the Center for American Progress) that could potentially meet the 49.5 % benchmark is New York, *Florida* (≈ 48 % in 2019), and *Maryland* (≈ 50 % in 2019) – all of which have smaller land areas than Ohio.

Thus **no state satisfies all three criteria**: Atlantic‑coast location, land area greater than Ohio, and a 2019 higher‑education attainment rate higher than Ohio’s.

None of the U.S. states that sit on the Atlantic coast and have a land area larger than Ohio qualify.  
Ohio’s land area is about **116 000 sq mi**. The Atlantic‑coast states all have smaller areas:

| State | Land area (sq mi) |
|-------|-------------------|
| Maine | 35 385 |
| New Hampshire | 9 104 |
| Vermont | 9 616 |
| Massachusetts | 10 554 |
| Rhode Island | 1 545 |
| Connecticut | 5 543 |
| New York | 54 169 |
| New Jersey | 8 722 |
| Delaware | 1 949 |
| Maryland | 12 406 |
| Virginia | 42 774 |
| North Carolina | 53 819 |
| South Carolina | 32 020 |
| Georgia | 59 425 |
| Florida | 65 755 |

Because none of these coastal states is larger than Ohio and the only state with a higher‑education attainment rate in 2019 (per the Center for American Progress) that could potentially meet the 49.5 % benchmark is New York, *Florida* (≈ 48 % in 2019), and *Maryland* (≈ 50 % in 2019) – all of which have smaller land areas than Ohio.

Thus **no state satisfies all three criteria**: Atlantic‑coast location, land area greater than Ohio, and a 2019 higher‑education attainment rate higher than Ohio’s.
